articles.title: ‘I’m always being real’: what on earth persuades disgraced people like Elizabeth Holmes to let the cameras in?
articles.summary: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives. But do they ever come out well?
body: That question of authenticity is at the heart of documentary film-making. You Can See Everything is as much about the ambiguous relationship between film-maker and subject as it is about Holmes herself. There is often a power struggle over narrative control in documentaries, with both sides of the dynamic wanting different outcomes from the final film. Watching You Can See Everything inevitably prompts the question: why would Holmes, days before she heads to jail, invite the scrutiny of a film crew?

Some people, like Holmes, think a documentary will help rebuild their reputation after public disgrace. When Anthony Weiner, who resigned from Congress after tweeting a photo of his bulging groin, tried to stage a professional comeback with a New York mayoral bid, he allowed cameras to film the journey. Only, he had more to hide: when further sex scandals emerged, his campaign went from a story of public redemption to innuendo-laden humiliation. And all the while, the cameras kept rolling. Weiner is a prime example of a subject losing control of the narrative.
points: With You Can See Everything, Holmes joins other such high-profile subjects as Lance Armstrong, Imelda Marcos and Anthony Weiner to allow film-makers to document their lives.

articles.title: Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Creator, author and SiriusXM host Tinx (real name: Christina Najjar) has been tapped to host the revival of reality competition series “The Circle” as it premieres next month on Hulu. “The Circle” previously aired for seven seasons on Netflix, where it was hosted by comedian Michelle Buteau.
body: Here’s the logline for the revival: “Reimagined as a fast-turnaround social experiment, Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ brings together everyday players and celebrities to compete side by side in a game of popularity where identity is ever-changing, and anyone can be anyone. Filmed in real time, the series gives viewers exclusive access as twists and player ratings unfold, with audience votes shaping the game. This fresh take supercharges the original’s signature mix of strategy and deception into an addictive experience built for today’s always-on audience.”

The series’ original conceit featured contestants living in different apartments and isolated from the outside world — and able to communicate through a social media platform dubbed “The Circle.” Over time, players were blocked until just one remained and won.

Tinx hosts the live SiriusXM call-in show “It’s Me, Tinx,” which premiered in 2022. The following year she wrote the book “The Shift: Change Your Perspective, Not Yourself,” which hit the New York Times bestseller list. In 2025, she released the fiction novel “Hotter in the Hamptons”; both books are currently in development for TV adaptations with Tinx as an EP on both.

articles.title: Scream review – Wes Craven meta horror remains super smart and scary 30 years on
articles.summary: Self-aware romp through the genre is redolent of the 90s but its ghost-masked killer is as alarming as ever. The 30th anniversary re-release of the original Scream, from screenwriter Kevin Williamson and director Wes Craven, brings us to a locus classicus of the 90s: a self-aware romp through the…
body: A ghost-masked killer is murdering and terrorising the bland Californian town of Woodsboro, and we begin with his gruesome assault on Casey (Drew Barrymore); he makes chilling calls to people’s landline phones, in an era where that meant you more or less had them pinned them down to a certain location. (The existence of “cellular” phones was still an exotic novelty.) The mother of teen Sidney (Neve Campbell) had been brutally killed previously, a crime pinned on local man Cotton Weary (a cameo for Liev Schreiber) who is now in jail. But was he really guilty? Now Sidney is at risk like everyone else.

articles.title: Making Marie Antoinette review – sweet Coppola home movie reveals the family business
articles.summary: Shot by Sofia’s mother Eleanor this documentary shows something of the strain of shooting a period piece, but is a far cry from the tumultuous portrait of her husband in Hearts of Darkness.
body: I t is 20 years since the release of Sofia Coppola’s Marie Antoinette starring Kirsten Dunst; it is a supportively unjudging, unironised study of the queen’s early years before the 1789 revolution, lavishly and accurately costumed, shot on location at Versailles and based on the Antonia Fraser biography – but also subversively and amusingly using pop tracks from the 70s and 80s on the soundtrack. It got a storm of booing from French critics, reportedly annoyed at the way their history had been reduced to a music video and fashion shoot with no French actors involved. Or hardly any.
points: Shot by Sofia’s mother Eleanor this documentary shows something of the strain of shooting a period piece, but is a far cry from the tumultuous portrait of her husband in Hearts of Darkness.

articles.title: MNEK cancels tour over lack of ticket sales and high production costs
articles.summary: The Grammy-nominated artist was due to start a run of shows for his latest album Bulldozer!! next month.
body: MNEK has cancelled his upcoming tour due to a lack of ticket sales and the show not being "ready to the standard" he wanted.
In a statement shared on Instagram, the 31-year-old said he joins other artists who have cancelled shows recently as a result of "high production costs" and "over-ambitious planning".
Earlier this year, The Pussycat Dolls called off almost the entire US leg of their reunion tour following poor ticket sales.
The singer, whose real name is Uzoechi Emenike, said he had been "really looking forward" to performing his new album but had "no interest in doing this tour if I can't do it right".

articles.title: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House review – new levels of giddiness unleashed in spooky spin-off
articles.summary: Picking up not long after the events of the final episode of the BBC’s haunted house comedy, this glorious new film is every bit as warm and comforting as the TV sitcom. What on earth is happening at Button House? Kitty has tasered a police officer.
body: Often when British sitcoms get a spin-off what happens is the gag-to-runtime ratio dips. But breaking out of the 30-minute episode structure seems to have freed up the writers to unleash new levels of giddiness with added spoonfuls of silliness. The jokes keep coming, and it’s every bit as warm and comforting as on TV.

articles.title: Glastonbury coach tickets oversold in admin error
articles.summary: Bookings will automatically be converted into a general admission ticket and coach fare refunded.
body: An administrative error resulted in coach journeys to the Glastonbury Festival being oversold through its official ticketing partner.
More coach package tickets were sold for certain departures than there are seats available, according to an email See Tickets sent to customers.
Those affected will not lose their tickets however. Instead, their booking will automatically be converted into a general admission ticket and the coach fare will be refunded.
The ticketing agency declined to comment further, but the BBC understands Glastonbury Festival was not responsible for the error.

articles.title: Don't Stop Believin' - high school musical Glee set for reboot
articles.summary: Ryan Murphy's popular musical comedy-drama is set to return on Hulu and Disney+ after a decade away.
body: We never stopped believin'... now it's official: Glee, the Emmy-winning US high school musical comedy drama, is set to return.
Ryan Murphy's series, which chronicled the highs and lows of choir members from Ohio, premiered on Fox in 2009 and ran for six seasons until 2015.
The original cast included Lea Michele, Amber Riley, the late Cory Monteith, Jane Lynch and Matthew Morrison as Will Schuester, the optimistic teacher leading the fictional McKinley High's glee club.
The reboot was announced, external by Disney and Hulu via the show's social media team on Wednesday.
points: Ryan Murphy's popular musical comedy-drama is set to return on Hulu and Disney+ after a decade away.
